headline: Four family members murdered in Rangpur; investigation transferred to DB, claims of sexual assault refuted
summary: The shraddha ceremony for the four murdered family members in Rangpur has been completed, as the case is transferred to the Detective Branch. Conflicting reports have emerged regarding evidence of sexual assault, with medical tests refuting an initial claim.
details: The shraddha ceremony for the four murdered family members in Rangpur's Masuapara was held on Tuesday, attended by priests, relatives, and local dignitaries.

caption:
A family of four, including a teacher, was brutally murdered in Rangpur. The case has been transferred to the Detective Branch amidst conflicting reports and public outcry.

The shraddha ceremony for the four murdered family members in Rangpur's Masuapara was held on Tuesday, attended by priests, relatives, and local dignitaries.

Relatives and locals expressed deep grief and anger, demanding a swift and accurate investigation to uncover the truth behind the brutal killings and bring those responsible to justice.

Rangpur City Corporation Administrator Mahfuz Un Nabi Don urged anyone with important information to contact law enforcement and asked for patience, allowing agencies logical time to investigate.

Don also cautioned against any attempts to divert the investigation or use the incident for political gain, urging citizens to remain vigilant.

Earlier, a mortuary attendant claimed to have found semen, suggesting sexual assault, but medical tests later showed no sperm, refuting the claim.

The murder case of the teacher's family has been transferred to the Detective Branch (DB) for further investigation, amidst continued public questioning of the initial police version of events.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star

headline_marked: [[Fertilizer dealer's license recommended for cancellation]] after farmers seize 225 sacks in Kurigram
headline: Fertilizer dealer's license recommended for cancellation after farmers seize 225 sacks in Kurigram
summary: An investigation found a dealer sold off 225 sacks of fertilizer instead of distributing them to farmers, leading to farmers breaking into a warehouse. Authorities now recommend cancelling the dealership.
details: Authorities have recommended cancelling a fertilizer dealer's license after an investigation found irregularities in Kurigram. This follows an incident where farmers broke into a warehouse and took 225 sacks of fertilizer.

The incident occurred at Shah Amanat Enterprise's warehouse in Bhurungamari's Dhaldanga Bazar on Sunday afternoon. The dealer, Taifur Rahman Mukul, had delayed scheduled distribution, causing a large crowd of farmers to gather.

A five-member committee, formed by the upazila administration, probed the incident and confirmed allegations that the dealer failed to distribute fertilizer to farmers, instead selling it through other business channels. Anomalies were also found in cash memos and registers.

The upazila agriculture office issued a show-cause notice to the dealer, but his explanation was deemed unsatisfactory. Consequently, the upazila administration decided to recommend scrapping Mukul's dealership.

This recommendation has been sent to the Kurigram deputy commissioner and will be forwarded to the divisional commissioner for a final decision. Meanwhile, Prime Minister's Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated there is no national fertilizer shortage.

Zahed emphasized that the government is ensuring production and addressing distribution irregularities, having approved the import of a large quantity of fertilizer. As of August 24, government warehouses held 13.656 lakh tonnes of various fertilizers.

The adviser acknowledged some problems with fertilizer distribution and announced that the government plans to change the system to benefit farmers. He noted that some dealers are not collecting their allocated fertilizer, causing localized issues.

Dealers have been strictly instructed to collect and fully distribute their allocated fertilizer. Additionally, a new three-member committee has been formed to review fertilizer lifting, distribution, and dealer appointments, providing recommendations to the agriculture ministry.
